title: Automated vendor-questionnaire triage with canned responses & evidence mapping
creator: Leah Ortega
description:
Problem: We receive an increasing volume of vendor/customer security & compliance questionnaires (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA, GDPR DPAs, custom vendor RFPs). Current manual triage by Legal/Security/CS results in slow turnaround, duplicate work, and SLA misses for enterprise customers. Redundant questions get answered repeatedly, and evidence artifacts live in scattered drives which slows responders.

Proposed solution: Build an automated intake and triage pipeline that: (1) ingests questionnaires (PDF, XLSX, Word, or web forms); (2) extracts structured Q&A using OCR/heuristics; (3) classifies questionnaire type and priority with a lightweight classifier; (4) matches questions to a canonical answer library and associated evidence artifacts; (5) generates a draft response with suggested answers and evidence links; (6) routes the draft to the appropriate owner (Legal/Security/Customer Success/Account team) with SLA timers and an explicit handoff UI for quick approval; (7) optionally returns a signed DPA template or initiates fast-tracked review for low-risk asks.

Goals & success metrics: reduce mean time-to-first-draft (TTFD) from ~72h to <8h for standard questionnaires; increase percentage of auto-resolved questions (mapped to canonical answers) from 12% to 60%; improve SLA compliance for enterprise questionnaire turnaround to 95%; reduce manual reviewer hours by ~40% per quarter.

Scope & constraints: initial scope targets common enterprise questionnaire formats (SIG, CAIQ-lite, custom vendor spreadsheets, DPAs). We will not automate legal negotiation for high-risk contractual terms in phase 1. Evidence artifacts must be referenced, not copied; access controlled via existing KMS and Drive permissions. A security review is required due to handling of contractual data and potential PII in submitted questionnaires.

Core components:
- Ingest: connectors for email, shared mailbox, Drive uploads, and a web intake form; document parsing pipeline for common file types and OCR fallback.
- Classifier & mapping: an embeddings-backed semantic matcher plus a small supervised classifier that selects question taxonomy + confidence score.
- Canonical answers store: versioned knowledge base with mapped evidence links (Drive/Confluence/GitHub PRs) and maintainers (Legal/Security owners).
- Draft generator: template engine that assembles suggested answers, includes evidence links, and flags low-confidence items for human review.
- Routing & SLA engine: routing rules (by question type, customer tier, geography) and per-ticket SLA timers surfaced in Console.
- Audit & telemetry: record full provenance, reviewer edits, approval timestamps, and redaction actions for compliance.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Parser extracts >90% of Qs from SIG/CAIQ-lite XLSX with correct question boundaries in 95% of test artifacts.
2) Canonical answer matcher returns a top-3 match where at least 1 match is correct for 60% of questions in the pilot dataset.
3) Draft response generation creates a reviewable ticket in Console with evidence links for >50% of questions for pilot customers.
4) Routing delivers drafts to correct owners and starts SLA timers; dashboard shows TTFD for pilot customers.
5) Security team completes review and approves storage/access pattern for evidence artifacts.

Rollout plan: pilot with two enterprise customers and internal Sales/legal teams (6 weeks), collect labeled dataset for matcher, iterate on answer library governance, then expand to broader customer base in phase 2 (Q2 2025).

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Aggressive automation speeds responses but risks incorrect answers being sent; mitigate with conservative confidence thresholds and explicit human approvals for flagged items.
- Evidence linking vs. copying: linking preserves single source of truth but requires Drive/KMS permissions; we need a short-term cached-read approach for high-volume reviewers.
- International data: GDPR/Schrems implications for evidence hosted in specific regions; routing must respect regional controls.

Documentation & controls to deliver: contributor guide for canonical answers, ownership RACI, sample templates for standard DPAs, and Console UI mockups for ratification.
comments: 2025-02-14: Scoping sync with Legal (Maya Chen) and Security (Omar Haddad). Agreed on phase 1 scope: SIG/CAIQ-lite, DPAs, and custom spreadsheets. Legal emphasized read-only evidence linking; Security requested KMS design before storing any extracted attachments.

2025-02-20: Prototype parser validated on 30 historical questionnaires. OCR fallback required for ~12% of docs; extraction accuracy ~88% on PDFs. Action: add OCR tuning and heuristics for tables by 2025-02-28. (Arjun)

2025-02-26: Decision to use embeddings semantic match + supervised classifier for taxonomy. Experiment: use a small fine-tuned SBERT model and index canonical answers. Data privacy note: all training data will be scrubbed of customer-identifying fields prior to model use. (Leah)

2025-03-03: Legal review feedback: include explicit review step before any DPA template is auto-sent; include change log for any canonical answer edits. Also requested retention policy for extracted questionnaires. (Maya)
2025-03-04: Blocker identified: need service account with limited Drive/KMS scopes to surface evidence links in draft responses. Security (Omar) to provide required IAM policy by 2025-03-10.

2025-03-05: Engineering estimate for MVP integration: 8 points across parser, matcher, and draft routing. Next steps: build ingestion webhook, wire classifier, and seed canonical answers with top 200 FAQ mappings. (Arjun)
